open_points.subject: A17 configuration and credential path traversal
open_points.question: What object is checked and read when skipping components leaves no final component, as with an empty path, `.`, `/`, or paths consisting only of those components?
options: Refuse because no file component remains
Treat the starting directory as the final object and then refuse it because it is not a regular file
Use the host's ordinary path-opening semantics instead of the stated skipping rule
open_points.default_guess: Refuse because no file component remains.

open_points.subject: A18 data-directory anchor
open_points.text: opened relative to the data directory it holds open from the start
open_points.question: How is the data-directory descriptor itself opened, and are symbolic links in the configured data-directory path, including the final component and its ancestors, followed or refused?
options: Open every component without following symbolic links
Refuse only when the configured data-directory path itself is a symbolic link
Resolve the configured path normally and apply the no-symlink rule only inside the resulting directory
open_points.default_guess: Open every component without following symbolic links and require the final descriptor to be the checked data directory.

open_points.subject: A18 failed store call after encountering a symbolic link
open_points.text: a link met so later makes that store call fail with nothing written
open_points.question: If the call published a file before encountering the link, must that file be removed, or may it remain as the unnamed published file that rule 3 expressly allows a failed call to leave?
options: Remove every file published by that call so literally nothing remains written
Allow an unnamed published file as rule 3 permits, interpreting “nothing written” as no committed record
Require all symlink-sensitive opens before any publication so the case cannot arise
open_points.default_guess: Require all symlink-sensitive opens before publication; otherwise allow no committed record but permit the orphan explicitly allowed by rule 3.

open_points.subject: A18 SQLite journal mode
open_points.text: in SQLite's default rollback-journal mode, which the kernel does not change
open_points.question: What must happen when an existing or restored SQLite database has a persistent non-default journal mode such as WAL, since the kernel neither sets the rollback mode nor defines a start check for it?
options: Refuse to start unless the database reports the required rollback-journal mode
Change the database to the required rollback-journal mode
Accept its persisted mode and extend the SQLite-file exception to that mode's files
open_points.default_guess: Refuse to start unless the database is already in the required rollback-journal mode.

open_points.subject: A18 SQLite-owned files
open_points.text: the journal being every file SQLite itself creates beside the database under the database's name
open_points.question: Which exact filenames or SQLite auxiliary-file classes are exempt from post-start symlink checks as “the journal”?
options: Every SQLite-created sibling whose name is derived from the database, including statement, super-journal, WAL and shared-memory files if they occur
Whatever files the linked SQLite build happens to open through its VFS
open_points.default_guess: Treat every database-derived sibling opened internally by SQLite as SQLite-owned, while requiring the configured rollback-journal mode to exclude WAL and shared-memory files.

open_points.subject: A20 supported Linux baseline
open_points.text: A release runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named
open_points.question: Which Linux kernel, architecture and userspace capabilities constitute a supported host, particularly for `O_PATH`, namespace creation, resource limits and the pinned sandbox runtime?
options: Support every Linux host and define failures when a required facility is absent
Name a minimum Linux/platform baseline for the release
Support only the release's build-and-test platform without a broader compatibility promise
open_points.default_guess: Support only the pinned release build-and-test platform and treat missing required Linux facilities as start failures.
